sections.title: The Theory Returns to One Life

figures.title: An embodied exchange
figures.alt: A living human Avatar exchanges experience and response with the Canvas. The Canvas carries an accumulated Painting. Little c, the local experiencer, remains distinct and is linked to the Canvas by access and update. The same roles are shown without placing consciousness at a measured physical location.
figures.caption: The Avatar embodies Little c in RF₀. The Canvas carries changing state; its Painting shapes interpretation and response. Little c remains distinct from the body and its carried state. Arrows show proposed functional relationships, not measured spatial connections.

figures.title: One moment changes the next
figures.alt: Seven connected steps form the Experience Loop: receive a moment; interpret it through the Painting; notice possible responses; form Intent; act through the body; encounter consequence; and carry change forward in Canvas state. A returning arrow brings the changed state into the next moment.
figures.caption: Follow one encounter through arrival, interpretation, available responses, Intent, action, consequence, and retained change. The return matters: the next encounter meets a changed Painting. This practical sequence does not establish DOT’s wider ontology.

figures.title: The proposed architecture
figures.alt: T × E, labelled Speculation, sits outside Big C and names its preexisting conditions. A large Big C enclosure contains an RF zero enclosure with the living Avatar, plus Little c and a Canvas outside RF zero. A one-way arrow labelled RS, Reality Stream, runs from RF zero to Little c. Little c exchanges access and update with the Canvas. Dashed arrows indicate continuing process. All shapes describe DOT’s proposed relationships, not measured locations.
figures.caption: T × E (Speculation) names the preexisting conditions for Big C. Within the model, Big C contains RF₀ and Little c. The Avatar embodies Little c in RF₀; Little c remains outside RF₀ and receives its Reality Stream. Boundaries show proposed relationships, not measured locations.

figures.title: RF₀ and the Reality Stream
figures.alt: Inside one Big C boundary, RF zero contains a living Avatar in a shared world. A downward Reality Stream arrow crosses the RF zero boundary and reaches Little c, which remains within Big C and outside RF zero. A connected Canvas carries the Painting used in interpretation. The frame is labelled lawful environment, the stream situated input, and the Painting accumulated interpretation. The diagram represents DOT’s proposed architecture.
figures.caption: RF₀ is modelled as a shared experience laboratory. The Avatar embodies Little c in the Frame. RF₀ supplies the Reality Stream; the Painting shapes its interpretation. Little c remains within Big C and outside RF₀. The diagram distinguishes roles, not measured spatial locations.

figures.title: Little c and local scope
figures.alt: Big C encloses RF zero and a separate local field of participation. RF zero contains the living Avatar and supplies a Reality Stream to Little c outside RF zero. Little c connects to the Canvas within a dashed field labelled local scope. Three lines state what can become more available as carried state changes: noticed distinctions, possible responses, and considered action. The local self-aware process keeps the same nature; scope describes access and participation, not size or rank.
figures.caption: Scope is the access and action available to a local perspective. As Canvas state changes, more may become available to notice, consider, and choose. Little c’s intrinsic nature is unchanged. The dashed boundary marks available participation, not physical size, rank, or a measured boundary of consciousness.

figures.title: Three roles in a changing life
figures.alt: Three panels repeat one visual motif. The first highlights the Canvas boundary as the capacity that carries state. The second highlights the accumulated strokes inside it as the Painting. The third shows repeated embodied actions as Character. The Canvas is not identical to its Painting, and neither is identical to Little c.
figures.caption: The Canvas is the capacity that carries and updates state. The Painting is the accumulated organization of that state. Character expresses patterns through repeated action. Highlighting a different part of the same drawing keeps capacity, content, and expression distinct.

figures.title: Connection and identification
figures.alt: Two panels show the same living body connected to the same Canvas and Little c. In the first, the thought is I am this reaction. In the second, it is I notice this reaction. The body remains visible and the arrows stay intact in both; no physical or functional connection is cut.
figures.caption: The functional connection is present in both panels. What changes is identification: a reaction may be treated as the whole self, or noticed as something that can be examined before a response. Practical decoupling keeps embodied life and consequence in view.

figures.title: When the field of choice changes
figures.alt: One encounter leads to two conceptual fields of response. In the narrowed field, defending dominates while asking, waiting, and setting a boundary are less available. In the wider field, asking, a boundary, waiting, and protection can all be considered. No response is scored and protective action remains a legitimate possibility.
figures.caption: DOT proposes that governing Fear can narrow which responses become available. A wider field can include curiosity, a boundary, waiting, or protective action. The drawing is a conceptual comparison, not a diagnostic scale or a claim that every imagined option is feasible.

cover.alt: Cover of Consciousness: A Digital Organism, Book One, by Henok Ghebrechristos. The theory diagram places T × E, explicitly labelled Speculation, outside Big C, the proposed conscious process. RF₀ and Little c are both within Big C. Little c is outside RF₀ and receives its Reality Stream. The living Avatar embodies Little c in RF₀. Little c, the Canvas and the Avatar remain distinct and connected. Broken arrows around Big C and Little c indicate process. Version 5.
